setupBody: Sets up Google Chrome with Chrome++ Next in {folder}. A Data folder already there stays as it is.
plusNotInstalled: Chrome++ Next is not set up
plusSetDLL: Loaded by chrome.exe through setdll, as {dll}
statusStaged: {version} is ready and goes in when Chrome restarts
statusUnsettled: Pitstop hasn't finished putting away the replaced version. It keeps trying.
statusWaiting: {version} will be applied after you close Chrome
runningBody: Close every Chrome window using this portable folder, then select Try again.
runningElevatedBody: Chrome is running as administrator, so Pitstop can't close it. Exit Chrome yourself, then select Try again.
busyBody: Another copy of Pitstop is changing this portable folder. Try again once it's done.
patchedBody: This chrome.exe was patched with setdll to load Chrome++ Next. A new chrome.exe would lose the patch, so Pitstop won't update or switch it. To let Pitstop update Chrome, run setdll /r chrome.exe in the App folder, then set up Chrome++ Next here.
backgroundBusy: Pitstop is updating in the background
rollbackNone: None yet. Each update keeps the version it replaces.
rollbackOff: Updates don't keep the version they replace.
switchBody: {current} is kept in its place, so you can switch back.
switchMilestoneBody: Chrome {version} is an earlier milestone than {current}. Chrome doesn't convert a profile back, so data such as History may not open. On a work PC, Chrome may restore its own snapshot instead, which deletes extension data and site storage. {current} is kept, so you can switch back.
deleteBody: You won't be able to switch back to this version.
doneStaged: Google Chrome {version} goes in when Chrome restarts
donePending: {name} {version} goes in after you close Chrome
activityClearBody: All activity records go, including the older ones not shown here. You can't get them back.
eventRecovered: Finished a change that was interrupted: {what}
updatesChannelHelp: Moving to a more stable channel doesn't downgrade Chrome. Updates resume once that channel catches up.
updatesKeepHelp: Updates leave the version they replace, so you can switch back. When this is off, the next update clears them.
updatesDiffHelp: Keeps the last Chrome package (about 500 MB), so that Google's server can send only what changed. If a differential update can't be used, the full update downloads instead. Turning this off deletes the package.
updatesHostHelp: Chrome updates download from this server first and switch to the other one if it fails. Automatic keeps the order Google's update server gives.
updatesPolicyHelp: Automatically and Ask before each update turn on in-app updates: Chrome++ Next starts Pitstop in the background with Chrome, and an update finishes through Chrome's own Relaunch to update. For this, Pitstop sets managed_updates=1 in chrome++.ini and adds its own command to launch_on_startup. Only when I check stays manual, and an update waits for Chrome to close. Pitstop then undoes both changes, and your own launch_on_startup commands stay. A change takes effect the next time Chrome starts.
askBody: Click to choose when to update, or to skip it.
askDetail: Restart Chrome to update now, or update the next time Chrome closes.
approvedBody: Pitstop will update {name} to {version} after you close Chrome.
installedBody: Click to start Chrome, or to open Pitstop, where you can switch back.
noInstallBody: Set up Chrome on the Overview page first.
iniMissingBody: Chrome++ Next uses its defaults. Create the file to change them.
pendingCount: {count, plural, one {# unsaved change} other {# unsaved changes}}
reviewDetail: {path} · {encoding}. Comments and order stay as they are.
changedOnDiskBody: Another program changed the file after Pitstop read it. Saving replaces those changes.
rawInvalid: Fix the invalid shortcut or key mapping to save.
invalidHotkey: Chrome++ Next can't read this shortcut. Set it again.
invalidTarget: Press a shortcut or choose a command.
nonASCII: This chrome++.ini has no byte order mark, so it can hold only ASCII characters.
optDataDirNote: Chrome uses the profile it finds in this folder.
optCommandLineHelp: Chrome gets these each time it starts.
optRunHelp: Each line runs through cmd. %app% is the App folder.
optBossKeyHelp: Works in any app. Hides every Chrome window and mutes Chrome. Press it again to bring them back.
optWin32kHelp: Turn this on only if Chrome crashes at startup with Chrome++ Next. Don't use it with MacType; exclude Chrome there instead.
optIgnorePoliciesHelp: Chrome skips the policies set in the Windows registry.
optSuppressUpgrade: Hide the false “out of date” prompt
optSuppressUpgradeHelp: Portable Chrome can't update itself, so it shows an update prompt that relaunching never clears. Real update warnings still show.
optDoubleClickClose: Double-click a tab to close it
optRightClickClose: Right-click a tab to close it
optRightClickCloseHelp: Hold Shift to get Chrome's menu.
optKeepLastTab: Keep the window open when the last tab closes
optWheelTab: Scroll over the tab strip to switch tabs
optWheelTabRButton: Scroll anywhere while holding the right button to switch tabs
optWheelTabRButtonHelp: Doesn't work while a mouse-gesture app runs.
optOpenURL: Open what you type in the address bar in
optNewTabDisable: Stay in the current tab when it's a new tab
optNewTabNames: Also count these tab titles as a new tab
optNewTabNamesHelp: A title counts when it contains one of these.
optHoverTab: Activate a tab by resting the pointer on it
keymapHelp: Turn one shortcut into another, or into a Chrome command.
cmdMoveTabToWindow: Move tab to a new window
cmdBookmarkBar: Show or hide the bookmarks bar
swNoDefaultCheck: Don't ask to be the default browser
swCacheSize: Limit the disk cache, in bytes
aboutBody: Set up, update and configure portable Chrome on Windows.
aboutPlusHelp: Makes Chrome portable and adds the tab and keyboard features
restartBody: Every Chrome window closes. Your tabs come back if Chrome is set to continue where you left off.
moveBody: From {from} to {to}. If it stays, Chrome starts with an empty profile.
moveBodyRunning: From {from} to {to}. Chrome is running, so Pitstop closes it first. If the profile stays, Chrome starts with an empty one.
cmdTabByPosition: Go to a tab by its position
